messages:
incident-bot: ALERT INC-4321 - toolcall throughput spike detected on prod region-us-west1. 95th p99 tool latency > 2s, tool.invoke QPS x4 baseline, error rate 8%. auto-escalate to oncall.
kevin_oncall: grabbing. any obvious deploys?
deploy-bot: recent deploy r2026.03.17-12:41 to inference-gateway (commit abc123)
maya_sre: looks like surge is mostly from heavy fncall flows with structured JSON outputs. KV cache miss rate up too. planning immediate soft mitigation: 1) reduce per-tenant tool QPS for free/dev plans to 1rps 2) disable structured output mode for best-effort tenants (fallback to text) 3) route high-latency tool calls to degraded CPU pool. thoughts?
kevin_oncall: do it. prioritize non-blocking for paid tiers. document exact commands so we can rollback.
maya_sre: commands: 
- feature flag: `ffctl set toolcall.rate_limit.plan.free 1`
- api gateway ACL: `kubectl patch configmap gateway-ratelimits -p '{"data":{"plan_free_tool_qps":"1"}}'`
- structured-output toggle: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" https://controlplane.internal/featureflags/structured_output/deactivate?scope=best_effort`
apply now and monitor 5m
kevin_oncall: apply and watch. leah_support, prep comms for customers who might see JSON->text fallback. include guidance and ETA.
leah_support: on it. drafting note: "During degraded conditions some tool-based responses will return text-only or limited JSON. We are actively throttling tool invocations for lower-tier plans to preserve availability. If you need uninterrupted tool access please contact support to upgrade." send to affected accounts list when we see stable bits.
maya_sre: mitigation applied: ffctl ok, configmap patched, gateway returned 202 for patch. now watching metrics: tool QPS down ~60%, error rate down to 2% at 30s, p99 latency trending down.
kevin_oncall: good. quick sanity: run smoke against a few tenant IDs that normally hit tool.invoke and confirm they get 429 or text fallback as expected.
tse_ops: ran through sample tenants: free-tenant-42 -> 429 on /v1/tool/invoke, paid-tenant-7 -> normal. structured outputs for free tenants now return text payloads with note header: "structured_output_unavailable".
kevin_oncall: mark incident as mitigation-in-place. start 30m watch. assign follow-ups: 1) eng-runtime to investigate KV miss and kernel selection anomaly (maya) 2) product to prepare targeted customer outreach for top affected accounts (leah) 3) infra to consider autoscale cushion for inference-gateway (tse_ops).
maya_sre: will open bug and link traces. initial hunch: r2026.03.17 changed batching heuristics, increased concurrent K cache churn.
deploy-bot: rolling back r2026.03.17-12:41 -> queued if requested.
kevin_oncall: hold on rollback for now, we have a working mitigation that preserves paid customers. only rollback if metrics degrade again.
leah_support: sending 1:1 emails to 12 affected accounts now, including steps to mitigate on their side and offer temporary credits.
maya_sre: additional low-risk change I pushed: limit tool.invoke fanout threads per model to 8 via runtime flag `max_tool_fanout=8`. applied to canary, will stage to region if no regressions in 10m.
kevin_oncall: monitoring. current plan: keep feature flag and rate limits until root cause addressed. if stable at 30m, we will relax free plan QPS to 3 and re-evaluate.
leah_support: customers responding, two tickets request SLA impact. I'm adding to incident doc.
kevin_oncall: ok handoff in 1hr to night oncall if still open. maya, tse please add runbook steps and rollback commands to the incident doc.
maya_sre: added runbook section with `ffctl rollback`, configmap restore snippet, and `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-gateway` for full revert.
kevin_oncall: thanks. ending active phase notes: mitigation reduced errors and latency. residual user-visible impact: lower-tier tenants see 429s on tool calls and JSON outputs replaced with text. please escalate if any paid tier regresses.
incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-4321 status updated -> mitigation_in_place. paging silenced for 1h.
kevin_oncall: closing thread here, will reopen if we see recurrence before handoff."
